text: EGOT is an acronym for the Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Awards, designating individuals who have won all four of the major performing art awards in the United States. These awards recognize outstanding achievements in television, audio recording/music, film, and theatre, respectively, and achieving the EGOT has been referred to as the "grand slam" of American show business. Including those with honorary or special awards, 27 people have achieved this status, with only Robert Lopez having won all four awards twice. The term was coined by actor Philip Michael Thomas in late 1984 while starring in Miami Vice, when he expressed a desire to achieve the EGOT within five years. The acronym gained wider recognition after a 2009 episode of 30 Rock introduced EGOT status as a recurring plotline. There is debate over whether only the Primetime Emmy Award should count, as some—including Thomas—consider other Emmy categories subordinate to the Primetime honor. Starting in 2016, the Daytime Emmy Awards had a category for Outstanding Musical Performance in a Daytime Program, which was removed after the 2019 ceremony because three of the four winners were Broadway ensembles, including five individuals (Cynthia Erivo, Rachel Bay Jones, Katrina Lenk, Ben Platt, and Ari'el Stachel) who already had Tony and Grammy awards and only needed an Oscar to complete their EGOT. In 2023, TheaterMania writer Zachary Stewart criticized the practice of "selling" producer credits for shows favored to win a Tony as a "shortcut" to EGOT status, distinguishing between producers who do the actual work and those who merely finance it, often late in the award season. American composer Richard Rodgers (1902–1979) received his fourth distinct award in 1962, with 10 competitive awards between 1946 and 1979; he was the first person to win all four and primarily a composer. Helen Hayes (1900–1993) received her fourth distinct award in 1977, with six competitive awards between 1932 and 1980; she was the first woman and first performer to achieve the EGOT, and the first to win the Triple Crown of Acting, with a 45-year interval between her first and fourth award—the longest among EGOT winners. Rita Moreno (born 1931) received her fourth distinct award in 1977, with five awards between 1961 and 1978; she was the first Latina and the first to win a Grammy as her second award, and became a Kennedy Center Honoree in 2015 and a Peabody Award winner in 2019; she is the second EGOT recipient and the first Hispanic actress to win the Triple Crown of Acting. John Gielgud (1904–2000) received his fourth distinct award in 1991, with five competitive awards between 1948 and 1991; he was the first to win a Tony as his first award, won his Emmy at age 87, and became the oldest winner, the first male performer, the first LGBTQ winner, and the first non-American. Audrey Hepburn (1929–1993) received her fourth distinct award posthumously in 1994, with four competitive awards between 1954 and 1994; she was the fifth person to complete the feat and the first to do so posthumously, and the first to win two awards in consecutive shows (the 1994 Grammys followed her 1993 posthumous Emmy), and is the only EGOT winner to not win multiple awards in any of the four fields. Marvin Hamlisch (1944–2012) received his fourth distinct award in 1995, with 12 competitive awards between 1974 and 2001; he had the most Oscars of any EGOT winner (three, all in the same year), won "General Field" Grammys in 1974 (Song of the Year and Best New Artist), and was the first EGOT winner to have won both an Oscar and a Grammy for the same work ("The Way We Were"). Jonathan Tunick (born 1938) received his fourth distinct award in 1997, with five awards between 1977 and 2024; he was the first EGOT winner to win an Emmy as his second award and the first to win the Tony as his fourth award. Mel Brooks (born 1926) received his fourth distinct award in June 2001, with 11 awards between 1968 and 2002; he was the first to win the Emmy as his first award and the first to win his Oscar for screenwriting; he is the only person to have won the Triple Crown of Writing, with an Oscar, Emmy, and Tony in writing categories. Brooks is one of only two people to have two awards of each type, though one of his Oscars was honorary; when he appeared on the January 30, 2015 episode of Real Time with Bill Maher, he called himself an EGOTAK, noting he had also received awards from the American Film Institute and Kennedy Center. Mike Nichols (1931–2014) received his fourth distinct award in November 2001, with 15 awards between 1961 and 2012; he was the first to win the Grammy as his first award, the first to win multiple awards for directing (an Oscar, several Tonys, and two Emmys), and has the longest timespan of awards among EGOT winners at 51 years; he is one of only two people (the other being Bob Fosse) to achieve the Triple Crown of Directing. Whoopi Goldberg (born 1955) received her fourth distinct award in 2002, with five competitive awards between 1985 and 2009; she is the first African American winner, the first to win the Oscar as her second award, and the third person after Audrey Hepburn (1954) and Marvin Hamlisch (1974) to win two qualifying awards in the same year (her Tony and first competitive Emmy in 2002). Scott Rudin (born 1958) received his fourth distinct award in 2012, with 21 awards between 1984 and 2021, tying with Alan Menken for the most competitive EGOT awards; he is the only EGOT winner who is solely a producer and did not win any of his four awards for a creative endeavor (singing, writing, acting). Robert Lopez (born 1975) received his fourth distinct award in 2014, with 12 awards between 2004 and 2022; he is the first Filipino and Asian to achieve the EGOT, the youngest winner (39 years, 8 days) to receive all four awards in competitive categories, and at the time the fastest to complete his qualifying run (9 years, 8 months), with a subsequent shortest interval of 7 years, 8 months (June 27, 2010 to March 4, 2018) until 2024 when Benj Pasek and Justin Paul surpassed it. Lopez is the first person to win each EGOT award twice; as of 2025, he is one Oscar away from becoming the first triple EGOT winner; he is currently the only winner to have two of each EGOT award in competitive categories, as Mel Brooks' second Oscar in 2023 was honorary; his first two Emmys were Daytime Emmys, followed by a Primetime Emmy in 2021 for WandaVision; he is the only EGOT recipient to follow a Daytime Emmy win with a subsequent Primetime Emmy win. Lopez received his Grammy for The Book of Mormon in collaboration with Scott Rudin, making them the first pair of EGOT winners to co-win the same award; he is also the first person to have won the Oscar last, sharing it with his wife Kristen Anderson-Lopez in 2014 and again in 2018; as of 2024, Kristen Anderson-Lopez lacks only a Tony to achieve EGOT status in her own right. Andrew Lloyd Webber (born 1948) received his fourth distinct award in 2018, with 12 competitive awards between 1980 and 2025; on September 9, 2018, he, John Legend, and Tim Rice simultaneously became EGOTs after being awarded the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Variety Special (Live) for Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert. Tim Rice (born 1944) received his fourth distinct award in 2018, with 12 awards between 1980 and 2018, sharing all awards with Elton John, John Legend, Andrew Lloyd Webber, and Alan Menken; on September 9, 2018, he, Lloyd Webber, and Legend became EGOTs via the same Emmy. John Legend (born 1978) received his fourth distinct award in 2018, with 21 awards between 2006 and 2025; he has the most Grammy Awards (12) of any competitive EGOT recipient, is the first African American man to achieve EGOT status, and the first person to receive the four awards in four consecutive years; he is the first EGOT recipient to have won both a competitive Primetime and Daytime Emmy, matched by Robert Lopez in 2021; on September 9, 2018, he, Andrew Lloyd Webber, and Tim Rice became EGOTs via the same Emmy. Alan Menken (born 1949) received his fourth distinct award in 2020, with 21 competitive awards between 1990 and 2020, tying with Scott Rudin for the most competitive EGOT awards; if his special Emmy is counted, he becomes the fully competing EGOT with the most overall awards; if EGOT status is recognized without regard to non-competitive awards, Quincy Jones holds the record with 30 fully competitive awards, including 29 Grammys; Menken has the most Oscar wins (8) by an EGOT. Jennifer Hudson (born 1981) received her fourth distinct award in 2022, with five competitive awards between 2007 and 2022, making her the youngest competitive female EGOT to date. Viola Davis (born 1965) received her fourth distinct award in 2023, with five competitive awards between 2001 and 2023, becoming the eighteenth person to competitively win each of the four awards; she acknowledged her new EGOT status while accepting her 2023 Grammy; she is the third EGOT recipient and the first African American actress to win the Triple Crown of Acting. Elton John (born 1947) received his fourth distinct award in 2024, with nine competitive awards between 1987 and 2024, becoming the nineteenth person to competitively win each of the four awards. Benj Pasek (born 1985) received his fourth distinct award in 2024, with seven competitive awards between 2017 and 2025, becoming the twentieth person to competitively win each of the four awards; he and Justin Paul set a new record for achieving EGOT status in the fastest time (7 years, 7 months); Pasek shares all seven of his competitive award wins with his writing partner Justin Paul. Justin Paul (born 1985) received his fourth distinct award in 2024, with seven competitive awards between 2017 and 2025, becoming the twenty-first person to competitively win each of the four awards; he and Benj Pasek set a new record for achieving EGOT status in the fastest time (7 years, 7 months); Paul shares all seven of his competitive award wins with his writing partner Benj Pasek. Six additional artists have received all four awards, though one was for an honorary or similar non-competitive distinction: Barbra Streisand lacks a competitive Tony; Liza Minnelli lacks a competitive Grammy; and Harry Belafonte, James Earl Jones, Quincy Jones, and Frank Marshall lack a competitive Oscar. Barbra Streisand (born 1942) received her fourth distinct award in 1970, with 18 awards between 1963 and 2001, three of which were non-competitive; at age 28, she obtained her fourth award with a special Tony, making her the youngest special EGOT winner; with only six years between her first award (1964 Grammy) and her 1970 Tony, she held the record for the fastest special EGOT until 2023 when Frank Marshall achieved it in four years. Streisand is the only EGOT to win an Oscar in both music and acting, and the only winner to have three competitive awards for debut performances (first studio album, first feature film, first television special); she also has the Peabody Award, AFI Life Achievement Award, Kennedy Center Honor, Cecil B. DeMille Award, National Medal of Arts, American Society of Cinematographers Board of Governors Award, and Presidential Medal of Freedom. Liza Minnelli (born 1946) received her fourth distinct award in 1990, with seven awards between 1965 and 2009, two of which were special. James Earl Jones (1931–2024) received his fourth distinct award in 2011, with eight awards between 1969 and 2017, two of which were special. Harry Belafonte (1927–2023) received his fourth distinct award in 2014, with six awards between 1954 and 2014, including a Grammy Hall of Fame Award and the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award (six special awards). Quincy Jones (1933–2024) received his fourth distinct award in 2016, with 33 awards between 1964 and 2024—the highest number of any EGOT winner; he won 28 Grammys, one Tony, and one Emmy, plus a special Grammy Legend Award and two special Oscars (Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award and Academy Honorary Award); his final qualifying award was a fully competitive 2016 Tony for The Color Purple. Frank Marshall (born 19) received his fourth distinct award in 2024, with nine competitive awards between 1980 and 2024, becoming the twentieth person to competitively win each of the four awards.

Between 1954 and 2014, American singer, activist, and actor Harry Belafonte (1927–2023) received a total of six awards, including a Grammy Hall of Fame Award and the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award, with two of those being special awards. He received his fourth distinct award in 2014. American record producer, musician, songwriter, composer, arranger, and film and television producer Quincy Jones (1933–2024) received his fourth distinct award in 2016. Between 1964 and 2024, Jones received a total of 33 awards—the highest number among any EGOT winner—comprising 28 Grammys, one Tony, one Emmy, a special Grammy Legend Award, and two special Oscars (the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award and the Academy Honorary Award). His final qualifying award was a fully competitive 2016 Tony for The Color Purple. American film producer and director Frank Marshall (born 1946) received his fourth distinct award in 2023. Between 2019 and 2023, Marshall received a total of four awards and is the only EGOT winner to have won a Sports Emmy Award and to have received the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award. With just four years between his first award (a 2019 honorary Oscar), a long format TV sports documentary, and competitive Grammy and Tony music awards, Marshall completed his EGOT collection in the shortest time of any person to achieve this status. As of July 2025, 74 living people are one award away from achieving (competitive) EGOT status. Additionally, 12 living individuals are one award away from achieving EGOT status, including those who have won at least one non-competitive award. As of 2024, 16 out of the 21 EGOT winners were American nationals, while the remaining five—John Gielgud, Audrey Hepburn, Elton John, Andrew Lloyd Webber, and Tim Rice—were British. There are conflicting definitions for the PEGOT: some define it as including the Peabody Award, others as the Pulitzer Prize. As of 2024, Mel Brooks, Rita Moreno, Mike Nichols, and Barbra Streisand have achieved PEGOT status via Peabody wins, while Marvin Hamlisch and Richard Rodgers have achieved it via Pulitzer wins. The REGOT includes a Razzie Award; Alan Menken has a REGOT due to his Razzie win (with Jack Feldman) for Worst Original Song for "High Times, Hard Times" from Newsies, and Liza Minnelli has a REGOT if her non-competitive Grammy Legend Award is counted. Lady Gaga reordered the acronym as EGORT after hosting Saturday Night Live and joking about her win for Worst Screen Combo (with Joaquin Phoenix) from Joker: Folie à Deux. Publications such as Vulture have listed the REGOT as including an induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame; Elton John is the only person with such a REGOT, though Harry Belafonte and Quincy Jones would be included if non-competitive awards are counted. In 2018, Leah Collins of CBC Arts proposed a Canadian equivalent of the EGOT—comprising the Canadian Screen Awards (and predecessors Gemini and Genie Awards), the Juno Awards, and the Dora Mavor Moore Awards—referred to by Toronto-based game show Trivia Club as the "Two-Can-Ju-Do," with no individual having won in all four categories. In 2019, Caitlin Welsh of Nova Entertainment proposed the "LAHA" as an Australian equivalent—Logie Awards, ARIA Music Awards, Helpmann Awards, and AACTA Awards—with no winners of all four awards identified, though Noni Hazlehurst has received nominations in all four.
